reanchor.note: ICD_ID is the surrogate identifier of a row in the ICD disease master, a reference/value-domain table keyed by ICD code with no policy/claim/member/assessment key. The only tagged anchor HUB_ASSESSMENT is a different entity and grain. Belongs to an ICD/disease master hub (REF) not tagged in Stage 3.

columns.rationale: Disease-master key, not the Assessment key; wrong anchor tagged.

reanchor.note: ICD_CODE is the business code of the disease-master entity itself. Satellite ICD-code attributes (SAT_CLAIM_HEALTH_DETAIL, SAT_RISK_HEALTH_MEMBER_MEDICAL) are per-claim / per-member instance grain; the grain rule forbids landing a master-keyed value on an instance satellite. Right anchor is a disease/ICD master hub not tagged.

columns.rationale: Business key of the ICD/disease master, not an attribute on an assessment/claim/member instance satellite.

reanchor.note: Descriptive name of the disease at disease-master grain. Look-alike attributes (Ailment Description / Condition Name) sit on claim/member instance satellites of the wrong entity and grain. Belongs to the untagged disease/ICD master anchor.

columns.rationale: Descriptor of the disease-master entity; wrong anchor tagged, no same-grain home in drawer.

reanchor.note: Classification of the disease at disease-master grain. No satellite in the drawer is parented on the disease/ICD master entity; all candidates are assessment/claim/member/party instance grain. Right anchor not tagged in Stage 3.

columns.rationale: Classification attribute of the disease-master entity; belongs to the untagged disease/ICD anchor, not an assessment satellite.

reanchor.note: BJAZ_HM_ICD_MASTER is an ICD diagnosis-code master/reference table; ICD_ID is the surrogate/business identifier of an ICD-code entry, not an attribute of an assessment. The only tagged anchor (HUB_ASSESSMENT) is an assessment-event entity of a different grain/entity. This code list is the value domain behind the 'ICD Code' attribute; it should anchor to an ICD/diagnosis reference, not HUB_ASSESSMENT.

columns.rationale: Master-table key for an ICD diagnosis code; belongs to an ICD reference anchor, not the assessment hub tagged in Stage 3.

reanchor.note: ICD_CODE is the business key of the ICD diagnosis-code master. The 'ICD Code' attribute on SAT_CLAIM_HEALTH_DETAIL / SAT_RISK_HEALTH_MEMBER_MEDICAL is that code AS USED on a claim/member (parent = claim/member), a different grain; the master itself is a REF value domain and should anchor to an ICD/diagnosis reference. HUB_ASSESSMENT (assessment event) is the wrong entity.

columns.rationale: Business key of the ICD code master; a REF value domain, not a per-assessment attribute — needs an ICD reference anchor.

reanchor.note: ICD_DESCRIPTION is the decode/name of the ICD code within the ICD master (REF value domain). It describes the ICD-code reference entity, not an assessment instance; belongs on an ICD/diagnosis reference anchor rather than any HUB_ASSESSMENT satellite.

columns.rationale: Decode of the ICD master code; attribute of the ICD reference entity, not the assessment hub.

reanchor.note: ASSOCIATE_CODE is a column on the ICD diagnosis-code master (e.g. an associated/owning code on the reference row); it does not describe an assessment event. With the whole table mis-anchored to HUB_ASSESSMENT, the concept belongs on the ICD/diagnosis reference entity (or a party/associate reference), not on an assessment satellite.

columns.rationale: A master-row attribute of the ICD reference; not an assessment attribute, so it cannot sit on any HUB_ASSESSMENT satellite.

target.key_derivation: tier1 on-view business code: HUB_CLAIM = nullif(trim(CLAIM_ID),''). Flat-relational source (Stage-0 reports no PARENT_KEY_HASH / FOREIGN_KEY anywhere and shred=null), so tiers 2-4 of the KEYING s1 ladder are unavailable by construction and no lineage walk may be invented. CLAIM_ID (NUMBER, sample 7631054) is the on-view canonical claim key; CLID_HPMS is a DIFFERENT identifier space (HPMS, sample 1063484) and is carried as a reference attribute, never as a second spelling of this hub (brief s4). Operand guarded per KEYING s9; a key that resolves to nothing must be REJECTED at build, not written as a bare prefix. ROW FILTER: DELETE_FLAG = '0' (brief s3.3 - only '0' is evidenced; 1=deleted is convention, not proof). This view carries NO Oracle versioning quartet (no VERSION_NO, no TOP_INDICATOR), so no version filter applies here.

key_reject_declaration.reject_rule: REJECT on a bare prefix or an empty value. One source operand, guarded nullif(trim(x),''), and where a namespace is present the outer nullif(...,'<NS>:') rejects the prefix-only value - essential on an Oracle source where 'NS:' || NULL evaluates to 'NS:'. Build predicate: emit the key only when nullif(trim(CLAIM_ID),'') is not null; otherwise REJECT the row - a hub key cannot be repaired after load.

augmentation.note: Per-head qualifier: the stated cause of death underlying the death head. No date, duration, count or condition attribute exists on SAT_CLAIM_BENEFIT_HEAD (its 12 attributes are code, description, coverage reference, four money/reason measures, sub-limit, co-pay, settled, status), and the concept is PER HEAD - so it cannot go on a claim-grained single-active satellite without keeping one head per claim. Proposed on the EXISTING multi-active satellite (no model change, no new satellite): parent HUB_CLAIM, declared child key 'Benefit Head Code' exactly as the model already declares it. [RR-C3 senior-mapper review 4.1] BENEFIT HEAD CODE VOCABULARY - RATIFIED RULING. SAT_CLAIM_BENEFIT_HEAD.'Benefit Head Code' is written by 77 blocks in this run from TWO source code spaces, and data_7.js declares the child-key NAME with NO value enum, so there is no model vocabulary to reconcile against: (1) BJAZ_HM_GPA_BILL_DTLS, 71 blocks, 12 values CHILD/CRITIC/DEATH/EDU/EMI/FAMILY/FUNERAL/HOSP/MED/PTD/TRANS/TTD. RATIFIED AS THE CANONICAL FORM. These are NOT mapper inventions: all 12 are the SOURCE'S OWN column-name prefix tokens on that view, verbatim and measured 12/12 (DEATH_BILL_AMT, TTD_BILL_AMT, CRITIC_BILL_AMT, ...). The head is encoded in the COLUMN NAME because the view is a flattened repeating group with no head-code column, so a literal per column is the only faithful rendering (KEYING s5 column_as_instance). Only the TTD row is value-sampled; the TOKENS are observed, the per-row VALUES are not. (2) BJAZ_HM_HCS_TECH_ASSESS_COV, 6 blocks, template {COVER_SECTION} resolved from a real value column (sampled 'CONVALBENCOV'). Also the source's own token, for a feed that DOES carry a head-code column. NEITHER SIDE IS REWRITTEN, and that is a deliberate refusal: no crosswalk between the two code spaces exists on ANY of the 35 in-scope tables, so rewriting either side into the other means INVENTING the mapping - the unrecoverable direction - and rewriting the 12 GPA tokens would additionally destroy observed source provenance to adopt an unobserved long form. key_reject_declaration.reject_rule: REJECT on the degenerate value only. A content hash is DEFINED over partial content, so a blank component is legitimate and each component is coalesce(col,'') BY DESIGN - in ANSI SQL NULL||'x' is NULL and an unguarded component would annihilate the whole hash input (KEYING s9.1). The s9 guard therefore sits at the COMPOSITE level and rejects the all-blank input. Do NOT 'fix' the inner coalesce: that would reintroduce the annihilation this shape prevents. Build predicate: REJECT when the normalised concatenation equals its own degenerate value (separator-only, e.g. '|||||||' / '||||', or empty after trim where the separator is a SPACE). Never hash an all-blank input; never key on the bare prefix.

The CODE side of the document-type decode (sample 1). BJAZ_HM_DOCUMENT_TYPES is a REFERENCE / DECODE MASTER: its two payload columns are the code and label sides of a document-type vocabulary. The model already carries that value domain as REF_DOCUMENT_TYPE, and the Stage-4 contract is explicit that REF tables are the value domains behind coded attributes and are NOT mapping targets here - only a source that IS a master maps to a REF, which this stage does not handle. target.key_derivation: tier 1, on-view COMPOSITE business code: (SCHEME_CODE '56440', PLAN_ID '94351'). PLAN_ID alone is not demonstrably unique outside its scheme, so both legs are carried; each operand is guarded nullif(trim(..),'') so a missing leg makes the whole key NULL and the row is REJECTED at build rather than keyed on a bare prefix (KEYING s9.2/s9.5). Namespaced 'SCHEMEPLAN:' - a contingency scheme plan is a distinct identifier space from a product UIN / PRODUCT_CODE and must not merge with them. SCHEME_VERSION is DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED from the key (Stage-3 finding F3): every definition version would otherwise mint a new hub instance and split the plan's satellites. The Oracle versioning quartet is ABSENT from this table (verified), but SCHEME_VERSION means the feed still carries more than one row per (SCHEME_CODE, PLAN_ID), so the build must filter to the current SCHEME_VERSION or carry it as a satellite child-key leg - the brief s3.2 hazard reaching a table the ruling does not name. [4b R5/C+B] Namespace retained (it separates a real population) and now guarded against its own degenerate prefix-only value, as every surviving namespace in this map is.

key_reject_declaration.reject_rule: REJECT explicitly rather than relying on NULL propagation. Operands are nullif(trim(x),'') directly inside the concatenation, so on an ANSI/Snowflake engine a single blank operand makes the WHOLE key NULL and the row is DROPPED SILENTLY - an unlogged data loss that looks like sparse source. ENGINE-DEPENDENT and NOT verifiable from the map: Oracle's || treats NULL as '' and would instead emit the sentinel 'SCHEMEPLAN:<code>|', i.e. the sentinel-live failure. The build must CONFIRM its engine's || NULL semantics and then apply the SAME rule either way. Build predicate: emit the key only when nullif(trim(PLAN_ID),'') is not null AND nullif(trim(SCHEME_CODE),'') is not null; otherwise REJECT the row to a reject log so the loss is counted.

Any earlier sentence below arguing for the channel hub, or for a namespace on that hub, is superseded by this line. [RR-C2 senior-mapper review 3.2, OVERTURNS 4b R10/A4] PARTNER: RESTORED. PARTNER_ID recurs on THREE in-scope tables (BJAZ_CTNGY_SCHEME_PLANS, BJAZ_INTERMEDIARY, BJAZ_PMSBY_DATA_WEB_SERVICE; a fourth, BA_TRV_DATA_POLICY_DTLS, is out of scope per review s0), which reads as a distinct partner/provider registry rather than a customer id; and an entity's FUNCTION (partner/payer) does not make its IDENTIFIER the same registry as the customer's. ONE spelling on every writer and on the LNK_PARTY_ROLE leg, byte-identical, per KEYING s4 - PARTNER_ID is NUMBER on all three in-scope tables and this run's convention for a NUMBER key is bare nullif(trim(...)), so no to_char is introduced. augmentation.note: SAT_CLAIM_STATUS_TRANSITION is proposed as a NEW single-active build-side satellite on HUB_CLAIM because a claim STATUS-TRANSITION log is a genuinely new theme for this anchor: all 45 existing HUB_CLAIM satellites were searched and none carries a previous status, a workflow process name, or the actor of a status change. GRAIN, STATED PLAINLY BECAUSE IT IS THE WHOLE DECISION: the source grain is one row per transition, and the model has no multi-active home for it. Run-wide ruling 3.2 offers two branches - filter to the current version, or put VERSION_NO into a child key - and I take the FILTER branch, so this satellite is single-active with one row per claim carrying the LATEST transition. multi_active is declared false and no child key is invented, because the only available discriminator is an ordinal and KEYING s8.1 demands a stability argument I cannot make from one sampled value. THE COST IS REAL AND IS REPORTED: under this branch the full transition HISTORY is not landed. Choosing the child-key branch instead would preserve it and would need a source answer on whether a claim version is immutable once written.

columns.rationale: TWO LEGAL READINGS, AND I AM THE OUTLIER I INHERITED. Run-wide ruling 3.2 makes the versioning apparatus a ROW FILTER, and Stage 3 reported that VERSION_NO is not-required on 5 of its 6 delivered occurrences and required on exactly this one - because here it appears ALONE, with no TOP_INDICATOR and no quartet, beside PREV_CLAIM_STATUS and CLAIM_STATUS, which makes it the only ordering the status history has. I carry BOTH: the filter is written into key_derivation on all seven rows of this view, AND the value is proposed as an attribute so the information does not leave the pipeline here. It is deliberately NOT made a child-key leg: it is an ORDINAL, KEYING s8.1 requires a stability argument for an ordinal child key, and I have none - a single sampled value of 8. If Stage 4 elsewhere prefers one verdict per column name, mine is the outlier and the cost of reversing it is that the claim status history loses its sequence, with UPDATED_ON still ordering it in time.

augmentation.note: three-plus parallel disability blocks on one row (PTD / PPD / FRACT / TTD / ADV), each a {description, percentage} pair, with the type living ONLY in the column-name prefix. The only model home, SAT_CLAIM_PA_DETAIL, is SCD2 SINGLE-ACTIVE with exactly one 'Disability Type' and one 'Disability Percentage', so routing even two of these there is a two-writer collapse (Stage-3 grain_risk). Proposed build-side, multi-active on (cover section, disability type). CROSS-SLICE: PTD_*, PPD_*, PPD_DESC_FUNC_LOSS and the TTD_* block are in the other slice of this table and must land on THIS satellite with their own type value [RR-C5 senior-mapper review 4.3, Stage-7 CT-01 APPLIED] MERGED. BJAZ_HM_HCS_TECH_ASSESS_COV was sliced across two Stage-4 batches and the halves independently proposed SAT_CLAIM_DISABILITY_HEAD (3 blocks) and SAT_CLAIM_PA_DISABILITY_LINE (14 blocks) for ONE concept; neither mapper could see the other. Decisive evidence they are one satellite is INTERNAL: 'Disability Description' AND 'Disability Percentage' were proposed on BOTH, same anchor, same view. CANONICAL NAME SAT_CLAIM_DISABILITY_HEAD - the 14-vs-3 block weight favours the other name but weight is the slicing ARTEFACT itself, not evidence; 'PA_' is product-line specific while this view's only sampled cover section is a HEALTH convalescence benefit, '_HEAD' matches this run's own per-section vocabulary on the same anchor (SAT_CLAIM_BENEFIT_HEAD exists in data_7.js), and '_LINE' would promise a line grain the child key does not provide. CHILD KEY = the 2-leg form 'Cover Section Code + Disability Type Code': the view is cover-section grained, so a Disability-Type-only key GUARANTEES a collision for a claim assessing one disability type under two cover sections, and adding the leg invents nothing (COVER_SECTION is present and populated). MEASURED SAFE: 17 blocks -> 17 distinct (attribute, child key) groups, every one a single writer, 0 collapses created; re-measured after the scope drop and confirmed by check_collapse.

augmentation.note: two structurally identical transport/provider blocks distinguished only by a column-name prefix (unprefixed vs ROAD_), with ROAD_AMB_TYPE and AIR_AMB_TYPE beside them naming the discriminator as transport MODE. Mapping both blocks to one provider name / address / contact attribute would be a two-writer collapse six times over. No model satellite holds a claim transport leg (SAT_RISK_MARINE_VOYAGE_LEG is the only Departure/Arrival pair and parents on HUB_RISK_OBJECT). Proposed build-side, multi-active on (cover section, transport mode). CROSS-SLICE: PROVIDER_NAME, PROVIDER_ADDRESS, STD_CODE and the six ROAD_* columns are in the other slice and must land here with mode ROAD / the same mode token [RR-C5 senior-mapper review 4.3, Stage-7 CT-02 APPLIED] MERGED. Same slicing artefact, worse: SAT_CLAIM_TRANSPORT_LEG (4 blocks) and SAT_CLAIM_TRANSPORT_PROVIDER (13) split ONE concept AND split the AIR instance across both, so the air departure/arrival sat on one satellite and the air provider name/address on the other while the ROAD equivalents of both sat on the second. Decisive internal evidence: 'Ambulance Type' was proposed on BOTH (AIR_AMB_TYPE / ROAD_AMB_TYPE). CANONICAL NAME SAT_CLAIM_TRANSPORT_LEG - it names the row's GRAIN (one transport leg per cover section per mode) where PROVIDER names an entity; provider-ness is already carried by the attribute names ('Transport Provider Name/Address Text/STD Code'). The 13-vs-4 weight is the artefact. CHILD KEY = 'Cover Section Code + Transport Mode Code', same grain argument as CT-01. THREE attribute names normalised, each diverging only by which slice mapped it: 'Departure Detail'->'Transport Departure', 'Arrival Detail'->'Transport Arrival', 'Provider Contact Number'->'Transport Provider Contact Number' (the last chosen for cohesion with its sibling 'Transport Provider *' set). MEASURED SAFE: 17 blocks -> 17 groups, 0 collapses created. OPEN SOURCE QUESTION, unchanged by the merge: all twelve transport columns are UNSAMPLED and the UNPREFIXED block may be the TREATING provider rather than the air leg, in which case the mode value is not AIR. That changes the LABEL, not the merge.

augmentation.note: two structurally identical transport/provider blocks distinguished only by a column-name prefix (unprefixed vs ROAD_), with ROAD_AMB_TYPE and AIR_AMB_TYPE beside them naming the discriminator as transport MODE. Mapping both blocks to one provider name / address / contact attribute would be a two-writer collapse six times over. No model satellite holds a claim transport leg (SAT_RISK_MARINE_VOYAGE_LEG is the only Departure/Arrival pair and parents on HUB_RISK_OBJECT). Proposed build-side, multi-active on (cover section, transport mode). CROSS-SLICE: PROVIDER_NAME, PROVIDER_ADDRESS, STD_CODE and the six ROAD_* columns are in the other slice and must land here with mode ROAD / the same mode token [RR-C5 senior-mapper review 4.3, Stage-7 CT-02 APPLIED] MERGED. Same slicing artefact, worse: SAT_CLAIM_TRANSPORT_LEG (4 blocks) and SAT_CLAIM_TRANSPORT_PROVIDER (13) split ONE concept AND split the AIR instance across both, so the air departure/arrival sat on one satellite and the air provider name/address on the other while the ROAD equivalents of both sat on the second. Decisive internal evidence: 'Ambulance Type' was proposed on BOTH (AIR_AMB_TYPE / ROAD_AMB_TYPE). CANONICAL NAME SAT_CLAIM_TRANSPORT_LEG - it names the row's GRAIN (one transport leg per cover section per mode) where PROVIDER names an entity; provider-ness is already carried by the attribute names ('Transport Provider Name/Address Text/STD Code'). The 13-vs-4 weight is the artefact. CHILD KEY = 'Cover Section Code + Transport Mode Code', same grain argument as CT-01. THREE attribute names normalised, each diverging only by which slice mapped it: 'Departure Detail'->'Transport Departure', 'Arrival Detail'->'Transport Arrival', 'Provider Contact Number'->'Transport Provider Contact Number' (the last chosen for cohesion with its sibling 'Transport Provider *' set). MEASURED SAFE: 17 blocks -> 17 groups, 0 collapses created. OPEN SOURCE QUESTION, unchanged by the merge: all twelve transport columns are UNSAMPLED and the UNPREFIXED block may be the TREATING provider rather than the air leg, in which case the mode value is not AIR. That changes the LABEL, not the merge.

augmentation.child_key: Cover Section Code + Disability Type Code
augmentation.note: PTD / PPD / FRACT / TTD / ADV are FIVE PARALLEL DISABILITY BLOCKS on one row and the only model home, SAT_CLAIM_PA_DETAIL, is SCD2 SINGLE-ACTIVE with one 'Disability Type' and one 'Disability Percentage' - up to five writers on one attribute. Declaring that existing satellite multi-active would be a MODEL CHANGE, which this run forbids, so a new build-side multi-active satellite is the floor. The discriminator exists ONLY in the column-name prefix (there is no disability-type column on the 109-column view), so this is KEYING s5 outcome 4 (column-as-instance): the child key must hold the disability TYPE (PTD/PPD/TTD/FRACT/ADV), never the raw column label and never an invented ordinal. child_key_value is left null for Stage 6 per the stage contract; the candidate values are published as a child_key_candidate finding. GRAIN CAVEAT: the view's row grain is (claim, COVER_SECTION), so if one claim carries the same disability type on two cover sections the single leg collides - COVER_SECTION may need to be a second leg (routed to Stage 6). 13 of the 14 columns are UNSAMPLED; the block structure is read from the names. [RR-C5 senior-mapper review 4.3, Stage-7 CT-01 APPLIED] MERGED. BJAZ_HM_HCS_TECH_ASSESS_COV was sliced across two Stage-4 batches and the halves independently proposed SAT_CLAIM_DISABILITY_HEAD (3 blocks) and SAT_CLAIM_PA_DISABILITY_LINE (14 blocks) for ONE concept; neither mapper could see the other. Decisive evidence they are one satellite is INTERNAL: 'Disability Description' AND 'Disability Percentage' were proposed on BOTH, same anchor, same view. CANONICAL NAME SAT_CLAIM_DISABILITY_HEAD - the 14-vs-3 block weight favours the other name but weight is the slicing ARTEFACT itself, not evidence; 'PA_' is product-line specific while this view's only sampled cover section is a HEALTH convalescence benefit, '_HEAD' matches this run's own per-section vocabulary on the same anchor (SAT_CLAIM_BENEFIT_HEAD exists in data_7.js), and '_LINE' would promise a line grain the child key does not provide. CHILD KEY = the 2-leg form 'Cover Section Code + Disability Type Code': the view is cover-section grained, so a Disability-Type-only key GUARANTEES a collision for a claim assessing one disability type under two cover sections, and adding the leg invents nothing (COVER_SECTION is present and populated). MEASURED SAFE: 17 blocks -> 17 distinct (attribute, child key) groups, every one a single writer, 0 collapses created; re-measured after the scope drop and confirmed by check_collapse.

All columns unsampled -- a naming proposal. Resolves 2 augmentation fan-in groups (Disability Description x3, Disability Percentage x2). augmentation.note: PTD / PPD / FRACT / TTD / ADV are FIVE PARALLEL DISABILITY BLOCKS on one row and the only model home, SAT_CLAIM_PA_DETAIL, is SCD2 SINGLE-ACTIVE with one 'Disability Type' and one 'Disability Percentage' - up to five writers on one attribute. Declaring that existing satellite multi-active would be a MODEL CHANGE, which this run forbids, so a new build-side multi-active satellite is the floor. The discriminator exists ONLY in the column-name prefix (there is no disability-type column on the 109-column view), so this is KEYING s5 outcome 4 (column-as-instance): the child key must hold the disability TYPE (PTD/PPD/TTD/FRACT/ADV), never the raw column label and never an invented ordinal. child_key_value is left null for Stage 6 per the stage contract; the candidate values are published as a child_key_candidate finding. GRAIN CAVEAT: the view's row grain is (claim, COVER_SECTION), so if one claim carries the same disability type on two cover sections the single leg collides - COVER_SECTION may need to be a second leg (routed to Stage 6). 13 of the 14 columns are UNSAMPLED; the block structure is read from the names. [RR-C5 senior-mapper review 4.3, Stage-7 CT-01 APPLIED] MERGED. BJAZ_HM_HCS_TECH_ASSESS_COV was sliced across two Stage-4 batches and the halves independently proposed SAT_CLAIM_DISABILITY_HEAD (3 blocks) and SAT_CLAIM_PA_DISABILITY_LINE (14 blocks) for ONE concept; neither mapper could see the other. Decisive evidence they are one satellite is INTERNAL: 'Disability Description' AND 'Disability Percentage' were proposed on BOTH, same anchor, same view. CANONICAL NAME SAT_CLAIM_DISABILITY_HEAD - the 14-vs-3 block weight favours the other name but weight is the slicing ARTEFACT itself, not evidence; 'PA_' is product-line specific while this view's only sampled cover section is a HEALTH convalescence benefit, '_HEAD' matches this run's own per-section vocabulary on the same anchor (SAT_CLAIM_BENEFIT_HEAD exists in data_7.js), and '_LINE' would promise a line grain the child key does not provide. CHILD KEY = the 2-leg form 'Cover Section Code + Disability Type Code': the view is cover-section grained, so a Disability-Type-only key GUARANTEES a collision for a claim assessing one disability type under two cover sections, and adding the leg invents nothing (COVER_SECTION is present and populated). MEASURED SAFE: 17 blocks -> 17 distinct (attribute, child key) groups, every one a single writer, 0 collapses created; re-measured after the scope drop and confirmed by check_collapse.

augmentation.child_key: Bill Line Type + Bill Head Code + Line Particular
augmentation.note: The claim BILL LINE has no home in data_7.js. HUB_CLAIM offers bill grain (SAT_CLAIM_PROVIDER_BILLING, childkey Bill Number), benefit-head grain (SAT_CLAIM_BENEFIT_HEAD, childkey Benefit Head Code) and a MOTOR parts line (SAT_CLAIM_PARTS_LINE: Part Category Code / Invoice Reference) - none is a health provider bill line. Decisive evidence: SAT_CLAIM_BILL_DIGITISATION carries 'Line Item Count', i.e. the model deliberately holds a COUNT of lines and not the lines themselves. Writing these line measures onto the head-grained SAT_CLAIM_BENEFIT_HEAD would keep one line per bill head (brief S6's GPA grid is genuinely head-grained; this family is not). Proposed build-side multi-active; the child key holds the line TYPE taken from the table/column-prefix identity, never the raw column label and never an invented ordinal (KEYING S5 outcome 4, S8.1). LEG RESOLUTION IS NOT UNIFORM and is declared rather than faked (CLAUDE.md: a named-but-empty leg is worse than an absent one) - see the per-row note. On THIS view: Bill Line Type resolves as the constant DISCOUNT (the table identity); Line Particular resolves from DISC_PARTICULAR_RAW; Bill Head Code DOES NOT RESOLVE - this view carries no bill-head column at all. BJAZ_NEFT_IFSC_MASTER is itself a REFERENCE MASTER and its canonical home is REF_BANK_BRANCH_IFSC (Canonical bank-branch reference keyed by IFSC for NEFT/RTGS/UPI), whose natural key is the tier-1 on-table IFSC_CODE, nullif(trim(IFSC_CODE),''). Recorded here so the key is not lost, per the rule that key work is never scoped by outcome. Flat-relational source: Stage-0 spine_present=false on this view and no FOREIGN_KEY/PARENT_KEY_HASH exists anywhere in the 39 tables, so NO tier-2 or tier-3 rung exists here (brief S2).

key_reject_declaration.reject_rule: REJECT on a bare prefix or an empty value. One source operand, guarded nullif(trim(x),''), and where a namespace is present the outer nullif(...,'<NS>:') rejects the prefix-only value - essential on an Oracle source where 'NS:' || NULL evaluates to 'NS:'. Build predicate: emit the key only when nullif(trim(IFSC_CODE),'') is not null; otherwise REJECT the row - a hub key cannot be repaired after load.

augmentation.note: BJAZ_NEFT_IFSC_MASTER IS a reference master, and data_7.js already carries its exact canonical home: REF_BANK_BRANCH_IFSC, 'Canonical bank-branch reference keyed by IFSC for NEFT/RTGS/UPI'. A REF table is a VALUE DOMAIN and is not a Stage-4 drawer target, so this is recorded as a REF-master build-side ROUTING ask for the modeller - the same disposition the brief S7 gives BJAZ_HM_STATUS_MASTER - NOT a missing-anchor gap and NOT a Stage-6.5 re-anchor. Deliberately NOT forced onto SAT_PARTY_BANKING (childkey 'Account Number Masked' - this view has no account number, and that satellite describes a PARTY'S ACCOUNT AT a bank, not the bank itself) nor onto SAT_INSTRUMENT_DEFINITION (which would mint one payment instrument per bank branch: over-anchoring, KEYING S3). NEW on REF_BANK_BRANCH_IFSC. NOT mapped to SAT_COMMON_ADDRESS.'City': the NEFT clearing centre is a payment-NETWORK attribute of the branch, not the branch's own city, even though both sample 'Bhilwara' on this row (brief S8: one shared value at n=1 is not proof).
